quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

2027-03-31.seasonLabel: Wednesday within the Octave of Easter

quote.text: All grace flows from mercy, and the last hour abounds with mercy for us. Let no one doubt concerning the goodness of God; even if a person's sins were as dark as night, God's mercy is stronger than our misery. One thing alone is necessary: that the sinner set ajar the door of his heart, be it ever so little, to let in a ray of God's merciful grace, and then God will do the rest.
quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

This rule we shall observe if we follow universality, antiquity, consent.
quote.author: St. Vincent of Lérins

quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

quote.author: G. K. Chesterton

quote.text: And so, Lord, do thou, who dost give understanding to faith, give me, so far as thou knowest it to be profitable, to understand that thou art as we believe; and that thou art that which we believe.
quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

quote.text: For thus we have been enriched by His poverty, the human nature having been brought up in Him to a God-befitting dignity, and established on thrones beyond all things.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria

quote.author: St. Gregory of Nyssa

quote.author: St. Ambrose of Milan

quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

quote.author: Tertullian

quote.author: Julian of Norwich

quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

quote.text: For the new grace of God has renewed all things from carnal unto spiritual, by superinducing the Gospel, the obliterator of the whole ancient bygone system; in which our Lord Jesus Christ has been approved as the Spirit of God, and the Word of God, and the Reason of God: the Spirit, by which He was mighty; the Word, by which He taught; the Reason, by which He came.
quote.author: Tertullian

2030-01-26.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Ferial readings of the day

quote.text: The Word of God, powerful in all things, and not defective with regard to His own justice, did righteously turn against that apostasy, and redeem from it His own property, not by violent means, as the [apostasy] had obtained dominion over us at the beginning, when it insatiably snatched away what was not its own, but by means of persuasion, as became a God of counsel, who does not use violent means to obtain what He desires.
quote.author: St. Irenaeus of Lyons

quote.text: For the beginning is faith, and the end is love. Now these two, being inseparably connected together, are of God, while all other things which are requisite for a holy life follow after them.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Antioch

2030-01-28.seasonLabel: Monday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
2030-01-28.celebration: St. Thomas Aquinas, Priest and Doctor

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. Thomas Aquinas, Priest and Doctor

quote.text: The presence of Christ's true body and blood in this sacrament cannot be detected by sense, nor understanding, but by faith alone, which rests upon Divine authority.
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2030-01-29.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: For nothing is more frigid than a teacher who shows his philosophy only in words: this is to act the part not of a teacher, but of a hypocrite.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2030-01-30.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Therefore it is necessary to arrive at a first mover, put in motion by no other; and this everyone understands to be God.
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2030-01-31.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. John Bosco, Priest

quote.text: The motive for loving God is God Himself.
quote.author: St. Bernard of Clairvaux

2030-02-01.seasonLabel: Friday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: If, therefore, those who were brought up in the ancient order of things have come to the possession of a new hope, no longer observing the Sabbath, but living in the observance of the Lord's Day, on which also our life has sprung up again by Him and by His death — whom some deny, by which mystery we have obtained faith, and therefore endure, that we may be found the disciples of Jesus Christ, our only Master.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Antioch

2030-02-02.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Thus it is that God, by loving us, restores us to His image, and, in order that He may find in us the form of His goodness, He gives us that whereby we ourselves too may do the work that He does, kindling that is the lamps of our minds, and inflaming us with the fire of His love, that we may love not only Himself, but also whatever He loves.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

quote.text: The believer has his stand on the Rock; for this reason he cannot be overthrown by the dashing of the billows.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2030-02-04.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: For the glory of God is a living man; and the life of man consists in beholding God.
quote.author: St. Irenaeus of Lyons

2030-02-05.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. Agatha, Virgin and Martyr

quote.text: Perfection is founded entirely on the love of God: 'Charity is the bond of perfection;' and perfect love of God means the complete union of our will with God's.
quote.author: St. Alphonsus Liguori

2030-02-06.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time
2030-02-06.celebration: St. Paul Miki and Companions, Martyrs

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. Paul Miki and Companions, Martyrs

quote.text: Paul, when enumerating the innumerable causes which generally separate men from the love of Christ and from the love of God in Christ Jesus, to all of which the love that was in himself rose superior, did not set down argument among the grounds of separation. For he says: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him that loved us.
quote.author: Origen of Alexandria

2030-02-07.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Man is created to praise, reverence, and serve God our Lord, and by this means to save his soul.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Loyola

2030-02-08.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Jerome Emiliani

quote.text: Conformity signifies that we join our wills to the will of God. Uniformity means more—it means that we make one will of God's will and ours, so that we will only what God wills; that God's will alone, is our will.
quote.author: St. Alphonsus Liguori

2030-02-09.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.label: Common of the Blessed Virgin Mary
formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Common of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Votive Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Collection of Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary

alternatives.name: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.text: Do not then go beyond yourself to seek for evil, and imagine that there is an original nature of wickedness.
quote.author: St. Basil the Great

quote.text: For as strolling, walking and running are bodily exercises, so every way of preparing and disposing the soul to rid itself of all the disordered tendencies, and, after it is rid, to seek and find the Divine Will as to the management of one's life for the salvation of the soul, is called a Spiritual Exercise.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Loyola

2030-02-11.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: Our Lady of Lourdes

quote.text: Almost all analogous names first were univocal and then by extension were rendered analogous, i.e. common by proportion to those things in which they are univocal and to others or to another. For example, the name wisdom was at first given to human wisdom and was univocal to the wisdoms of all men. Then, when men rose to a knowledge of the divine nature and saw the proportional similitude between us insofar as we are wise and God, they extended the name wisdom to signify in God that to which our wisdom is proportional.
quote.author: Thomas Cajetan (Cardinal de Vio)

2030-02-12.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Nothing is worse than envy and malice, nothing more mischievous than vainglory; it is wont to mar ten thousand good things.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2030-02-13.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: The Christian mysteries are an indivisible whole. The way from Bethlehem leads inevitably to Golgotha, from the crib to the Cross. The star of Bethlehem shines in the night of sin. The shadow of the Cross falls on the light that shines from the crib. This light is extinguished in the darkness of Good Friday, but it rises all the more brilliantly in the sun of grace on the morning of the Resurrection.
quote.author: St. Edith Stein (Teresa Benedicta of the Cross)

2030-02-14.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: Sts. Cyril and Methodius

quote.text: Don't wish to be like the gilded weather-cock on top of a great building: however much it shines, and however high it stands, it adds nothing to the solidity of the building. Rather be like an old stone block hidden in the foundations, underground, where no one can see you: because of you the house will not fall.
quote.author: St. Josemaría Escrivá

2030-02-15.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour?
quote.author: St. Polycarp of Smyrna

2030-02-16.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.label: Common of the Blessed Virgin Mary
formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Common of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.label: Votive Mass of the Blessed Virgin Mary
formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Votive Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.label: Collection of Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary
formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Collection of Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary

alternatives.name: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.text: Christ is of those who are humble-minded, and not of those who exalt themselves over His flock. Our Lord Jesus Christ, the Sceptre of the majesty of God, did not come in the pomp of pride or arrogance, although He might have done so, but in a lowly condition, as the Holy Spirit had declared regarding Him.
quote.author: St. Clement of Rome

quote.text: For a dreadful, a dreadful thing is the love of money, it disables both eyes and ears, and makes men worse to deal with than a wild beast, allowing a man to consider neither conscience, nor friendship, nor fellowship, nor the salvation of his own soul.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2030-02-18.seasonLabel: Monday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: For peace is a good so great, that even in this earthly and mortal life there is no word we hear with such pleasure, nothing we desire with such zest, or find to be more thoroughly gratifying.
quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

2030-02-19.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Let us beg of God, who causes those who are of one mind to live in his Father's house, that He will vouchsafe, by his heavenly tokens, to declare to us, which tradition is to be followed; and by what means we are to find our way to his heavenly kingdom.
quote.author: St. Bede the Venerable

2030-02-20.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Where hast Thou hidden Thyself, And abandoned me to my sorrow, O my Beloved! Thou hast fled like the hart, Having wounded me. I ran after Thee, crying; but Thou wert gone.
quote.author: St. John of the Cross

2030-02-21.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Peter Damian, Bishop and Doctor

alternatives.name: St. Peter Damian, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: For faith is to believe what thou yet seest not; and the reward of faith is, to see what thou believest.
quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

2030-02-22.seasonLabel: Friday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time
2030-02-22.celebration: The Chair of St. Peter, Apostle

quote.text: This Good is celebrated by the sacred theologians, both as beautiful and as Beauty, and as Love, and as Beloved; and all the other Divine Names which beseem the beautifying and highly-favoured comeliness.
quote.author: (Pseudo-Dionysius)

2030-02-23.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. Polycarp, Bishop and Martyr

quote.text: May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ Himself, who is the Son of God, and our everlasting High Priest, build you up in faith and truth, and in all meekness, gentleness, patience, long-suffering, forbearance, and purity; and may He bestow on you a lot and portion among His saints, and on us with you, and on all that are under heaven, who shall believe in our Lord Jesus Christ.
quote.author: St. Polycarp of Smyrna

quote.text: The soul in which God dwells by grace is no impersonal scene of the divine life but is itself drawn into this life. The divine life is three-personal life: it is overflowing love, in which the Father generates the Son and gives him his Being, while the Son embraces this Being and returns it to the Father; it is the love in which the Father and Son are one, both breathing the Holy Spirit. By grace this Spirit is shed abroad in men's hearts.
quote.author: St. Edith Stein (Teresa Benedicta of the Cross)

2030-02-25.seasonLabel: Monday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: There are two ways, one of life and one of death; but a great difference between the two ways. The way of life, then, is this: First, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbour as yourself; and all things whatsoever you would should not occur to you, do not also do to another.
quote.author: The Didache

2030-02-26.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: By no means then is it permitted to speak, or even to think, anything, concerning the superessential and hidden Deity, beyond those things divinely revealed to us in the sacred Oracles.
quote.author: (Pseudo-Dionysius)

2030-02-27.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

unavailableFormularies.celebrationName: St. Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor

alternatives.name: St. Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor

quote.text: And more than all other men are we your helpers and allies in promoting peace, seeing that we hold this view, that it is alike impossible for the wicked, the covetous, the conspirator, and for the virtuous, to escape the notice of God, and that each man goes to everlasting punishment or salvation according to the value of his actions.
quote.author: St. Justin Martyr

2030-02-28.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Beneficially, therefore, did the divine Mercy provide that it should instruct us to hold by faith even those truths that the human reason is able to investigate.
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2030-03-01.seasonLabel: Friday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: The greatest challenge of the day is: how to bring about a revolution of the heart, a revolution which has to start with each one of us?
quote.author: Servant of God Dorothy Day

2030-03-02.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Common of the Blessed Virgin Mary

formularyOptions.label: Collection of Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary
formularyOptions.lectionaryReference: Collection of Masses of the Blessed Virgin Mary

alternatives.name: Saturday Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.text: Without faith it is impossible to be saved.
quote.author: St. John of Damascus

quote.text: Grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2030-03-04.seasonLabel: Monday of the Eighth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Casimir

quote.text: Hearken, O my son, to the precepts of thy master, and incline the ear of thine heart.
quote.author: St. Benedict of Nursia

2030-03-05.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Eighth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: For all things in the eye of God are second to love.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

quote.text: Fasting is the soul of prayer, mercy is the lifeblood of fasting. Let no one try to separate them; they cannot be separated. If you have only one of them or not all together, you have nothing. So if you pray, fast; if you fast, show mercy; if you want your petition to be heard, hear the petition of others.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

quote.text: It is only by conforming our own will to the divine one that human beings attain their true height, that they become 'divine'; only by coming out of ourselves, only in the 'yes' to God, is Adam's desire — and the desire of us all — to be completely free.
quote.author: Pope Benedict XVI

quote.text: More easily through fasting does prayer penetrate heaven.
quote.author: St. Isidore of Seville

quote.text: Take my advice, my friend, and be slow to do evil, but swift to your salvation; for readiness to evil and tardiness to good are equally bad.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

quote.text: If you don't deny yourself you will never be a soul of prayer.
quote.author: St. Josemaría Escrivá

2030-03-11.seasonLabel: Monday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: O sweet Jesus, wound my heart, that tears of penitence and love may be my food night and day, and bring me entirely to thee; that my heart may ever be habitable for thee, and my conversation pleasing and acceptable to thee; and the end of my life so praiseworthy, that after the close of this life, I may deserve to praise thee with all thy Saints forever.
quote.author: St. Bridget of Sweden

2030-03-12.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: A soul does not benefit as it should from the sacrament of confession if it is not humble. Pride keeps it in darkness. The soul neither knows how, nor is it willing, to probe with precision the depths of its own misery. It puts on a mask and avoids everything that might bring it recovery.
quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

2030-03-13.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: From this love-o'erflowing Passion, I take what fully makes up for the insufficiency of my own small merits; herein lies my complete justification; to meditate on this Passion, I call eternal wisdom, the perfection of all knowledge, the riches of all salvation, an entire satisfaction of all desert; it casts me down in prosperity, it raises me up in adversity, it keeps me in an even balance between this world's weal and woe, and guards me against all evil in complete security.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2030-03-14.seasonLabel: Thursday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: Turn thee with thy whole heart unto the Lord, and forsake this wretched world, and thy soul shall find rest. Learn to despise outward things and to give thyself to things inward, and thou shalt see the kingdom of God come within thee.
quote.author: Thomas à Kempis

2030-03-15.seasonLabel: Friday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: So it behoves us, if we would have Christ for a frequent guest, to fill our hearts with faithful meditations on the mercy He showed in dying for us, and on His mighty power in rising again from the dead.
quote.author: St. Bernard of Clairvaux

2030-03-16.seasonLabel: Saturday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: Do you fast? Give me proof of it by your works. If you see a poor man, take pity on him.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

quote.text: Behold, assiduous meditation on My Passion makes out of a simple man a master of high knowledge; truly it is a living book in which everything is to be found. How right blessed is that man who has it ever before his eyes and studies it!
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2030-03-18.seasonLabel: Monday of the Second Week of Lent

alternatives.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: Dost thou not know, dear daughter, that all the sufferings, which the soul endures, or can endure, in this life, are insufficient to punish one smallest fault, because the offence, being done to Me, who am the Infinite Good, calls for an infinite satisfaction?
quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

2030-03-19.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Second Week of Lent
2030-03-19.celebration: St. Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.text: He who had wished to demonstrate to us, even in His own flesh, the flesh's infirmity, by the reality of suffering, said, 'Father, remove this Your cup'; and remembering Himself, added, 'save that not my will, but Yours be done.' He was the Will and the Power of the Father: and yet, for the demonstration of the patience which was due, He gave Himself up to the Father's Will.
quote.author: Tertullian

2030-03-20.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: When the body therefore fasts from food, let the mind fast from vices, and pass judgment upon all earthly cares and desires according to the law of its King.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

2030-03-21.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: Whoever is desirous of great reward and everlasting salvation, of high knowledge and deep wisdom, of standing erect in joy and sorrow, of possessing full security against all evil, whoever wishes to drink a draught of Thy bitter Passion, and Thy singular sweetness, must carry Thee at all times, O crucified Jesus, before the eyes of his heart.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2030-03-22.seasonLabel: Friday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: Take therefore first, as an indestructible foundation, the Cross, and build upon it the other articles of the faith.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

2030-03-23.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: God was born to take us into Himself, suffered to justify us, and died to avenge us; for our manhood abides for ever in Him, the weakness of our infirmity is united with His strength, and the spiritual powers of iniquity and wickedness are subdued in the triumph of our flesh, since God died through the flesh.
quote.author: St. Hilary of Poitiers

quote.text: Go and sit in your cell and your cell will teach you everything.
quote.author: Abba Moses

2030-03-25.seasonLabel: Monday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: As you have entered upon a good and most glorious path, run with reverence the race of godliness.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

2030-03-26.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: Strive always to prefer, not that which is easiest, but that which is most difficult; Not that which is most delectable, but that which is most unpleasing; Not that which gives most pleasure, but rather that which gives least; Not that which is restful, but that which is wearisome.
quote.author: St. John of the Cross

2030-03-27.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: O Lord and Master of my life, give me not the spirit of sloth, of despondency, of ambition, or of idle talking; but bestow on me, Thy servant, the spirit of chastity, of humility, of patience, and of love.
quote.author: St. Ephrem the Syrian

2030-03-28.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: The whole of our treatment and exertion is concerned with the hidden man of the heart, and our warfare is directed against that adversary and foe within us, who uses ourselves as his weapons against ourselves, and, most fearful of all, hands us over to the death of sin.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

2030-03-29.seasonLabel: Friday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: Offer your soul to God, make him an oblation of your fasting, so that your soul may be a pure offering, a holy sacrifice, a living victim, remaining your own and at the same time made over to God. Whoever fails to give this to God will not be excused, for if you are to give him yourself you are never without the means of giving.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

2030-03-30.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: A man is born natural and physical. In baptism he becomes supernatural and theological.
quote.author: St. Lawrence of Brindisi

quote.text: Oh, what a sure path is the way of Thy Passion, along the way of truth, up to the very pinnacle of all perfection.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2030-04-01.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: O sweet exchange! O unsearchable operation! O benefits surpassing all expectation! That the wickedness of many should be hid in a single righteous One, and that the righteousness of One should justify many transgressors!
quote.author: Author of the Epistle to Diognetus

2030-04-02.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: In the distribution of alms and care of the poor, let our Christian fast-times be fat and abound; and let each bestow on the weak and destitute those dainties which he denies himself.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

2030-04-03.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: There are three things, my brethren, by which faith stands firm, devotion remains constant, and virtue endures. They are prayer, fasting and mercy. Prayer knocks at the door, fasting obtains, mercy receives. Prayer, mercy and fasting: these three are one, and they give life to each other.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

2030-04-04.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: The sixth, to consider how He suffers all this for my sins, etc.; and what I ought to do and suffer for Him.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Loyola

2030-04-05.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: For that death is destroyed, and that the Cross has become the victory over it, and that it has no more power but is verily dead, this is no small proof, or rather an evident warrant, that it is despised by all Christ's disciples, and that they all take the aggressive against it and no longer fear it; but by the sign of the Cross and by faith in Christ tread it down as dead.
quote.author: St. Athanasius

2030-04-06.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: Let us then not be ashamed of the Cross of our Saviour, but rather glory in it.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

quote.text: For the wilderness is the mother of quiet; it is a calm and a harbor, delivering us from all turmoils.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2030-04-08.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: For if we too live as though dying daily, we shall not sin.
quote.author: St. Athanasius

2030-04-09.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: Wherefore virtue has need at our hands of willingness alone, since it is in us and is formed from us.
quote.author: St. Athanasius

2030-04-10.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: As soon as a man seriously seeks truth and goodness, this intimate conversation with himself tends to become conversation with God. Little by little, instead of seeking himself in everything, instead of tending more or less consciously to make himself a center, man tends to seek God in everything, and to substitute for egoism love of God and of souls in Him. This constitutes the interior life.
quote.author: Fr. Reginald Garrigou-Lagrange, O.P.

2030-04-11.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: It is better for a man to be silent and be [a Christian], than to talk and not to be one. It is good to teach, if he who speaks also acts. There is then one Teacher, who spoke and it was done; while even those things which He did in silence are worthy of the Father.
quote.author: St. Ignatius of Antioch

2030-04-12.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: She is not only human; she is humanity. The one thing that she did and does is the one thing that we all have to do, namely, to bear Christ into the world.
quote.author: Caryll Houselander

2030-04-13.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Lent

alternatives.name: St. Martin I, Pope and Martyr

quote.text: There is nothing more pleasing we can offer God than to say to him: 'Possess thyself of us.'
quote.author: St. Louis de Montfort

2030-04-14.celebration: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord

quote.text: Christianity is the only frame for pagan freedom.
quote.author: G. K. Chesterton

quote.text: This is the way, beloved, in which we find our Saviour, even Jesus Christ, the High Priest of all our offerings, the defender and helper of our infirmity. By Him we look up to the heights of heaven. By Him we behold, as in a glass, His immaculate and most excellent visage. By Him are the eyes of our hearts opened. By Him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms up anew towards His marvellous light.
quote.author: St. Clement of Rome

quote.text: The will, therefore, is then truly free, when it is not the slave of vices and sins. Such was it given us by God; and this being lost by its own fault, can only be restored by Him who was able at first to give it. And therefore the truth says, If the Son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed.
quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

quote.text: For our life in this sojourning cannot be without temptation: because our advance is made through our temptation, nor does a man become known to himself unless tempted, nor can he be crowned except he shall have conquered, nor can he conquer except he shall have striven, nor can he strive except he shall have experienced an enemy, and temptations.
quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

2030-04-18.celebration: Holy Thursday — Mass of the Lord's Supper

readingOptions.label: Chrism Mass (morning)

quote.text: No indeed, my child, the devotion which is true hinders nothing, but on the contrary it perfects everything; and that which runs counter to the rightful vocation of any one is, you may be sure, a spurious devotion.
quote.author: St. Francis de Sales

2030-04-19.celebration: Good Friday of the Passion of the Lord

quote.text: Those who love God are always happy, because their whole happiness is to fulfill, even in adversity, the will of God.
quote.author: St. Alphonsus Liguori

alternatives.name: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order

quote.text: Man is called to a fullness of life which far exceeds the dimensions of his earthly existence, because it consists in sharing the very life of God.
quote.author: St. John Paul II

2031-02-18.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Charity is the form of the virtues.
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2031-02-19.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Where hast Thou hidden Thyself, And abandoned me to my sorrow, O my Beloved! Thou hast fled like the hart, Having wounded me. I ran after Thee, crying; but Thou wert gone.
quote.author: St. John of the Cross

2031-02-20.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: The common belief of all mankind agrees that God, the supreme of all things, is good. For since nothing can be imagined better than God, how can we doubt Him to be good than whom there is nothing better?
quote.author: St. Boethius

2031-02-21.seasonLabel: Friday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Peter Damian, Bishop and Doctor

alternatives.name: St. Peter Damian, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: Perfection is founded entirely on the love of God: 'Charity is the bond of perfection;' and perfect love of God means the complete union of our will with God's.
quote.author: St. Alphonsus Liguori

2031-02-22.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: A person enters into the first tabernacle when he returns to himself. A person enters into the second tabernacle when he goes beyond himself. When going beyond himself surely a person is elevated to God.
quote.author: Richard of St. Victor

quote.text: The beginning of discipline is humility: first, that he hold no knowledge, no scripture as vile; second, that he not be ashamed to learn from anyone; third, that when he shall have attained knowledge, he not contemn the others.
quote.author: Hugh of St. Victor

2031-02-24.seasonLabel: Monday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: All waters, therefore, in virtue of the pristine privilege of their origin, do, after invocation of God, attain the sacramental power of sanctification; for the Spirit immediately supervenes from the heavens, and rests over the waters, sanctifying them from Himself.
quote.author: Tertullian

2031-02-25.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time

quote.text: Nobody will begin to understand the Thomist philosophy, or indeed the Catholic philosophy, who does not realise that the primary and fundamental part of it is entirely the praise of Life, the praise of Being, the praise of God as the Creator of the World.
quote.author: G. K. Chesterton

quote.text: If you don't deny yourself you will never be a soul of prayer.
quote.author: St. Josemaría Escrivá

unavailableFormularies.celebrationName: St. Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor

alternatives.name: St. Gregory of Narek, Abbot and Doctor

quote.text: God was born to take us into Himself, suffered to justify us, and died to avenge us; for our manhood abides for ever in Him, the weakness of our infirmity is united with His strength, and the spiritual powers of iniquity and wickedness are subdued in the triumph of our flesh, since God died through the flesh.
quote.author: St. Hilary of Poitiers

quote.text: Turn thee with thy whole heart unto the Lord, and forsake this wretched world, and thy soul shall find rest. Learn to despise outward things and to give thyself to things inward, and thou shalt see the kingdom of God come within thee.
quote.author: Thomas à Kempis

quote.text: Fasting is the soul of prayer, mercy is the lifeblood of fasting. Let no one try to separate them; they cannot be separated. If you have only one of them or not all together, you have nothing. So if you pray, fast; if you fast, show mercy; if you want your petition to be heard, hear the petition of others.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

quote.text: When the body therefore fasts from food, let the mind fast from vices, and pass judgment upon all earthly cares and desires according to the law of its King.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

2031-03-03.seasonLabel: Monday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: We needed an Incarnate God, a God put to death, that we might live.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

2031-03-04.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: There are three things, my brethren, by which faith stands firm, devotion remains constant, and virtue endures. They are prayer, fasting and mercy. Prayer knocks at the door, fasting obtains, mercy receives. Prayer, mercy and fasting: these three are one, and they give life to each other.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

2031-03-05.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: As you have entered upon a good and most glorious path, run with reverence the race of godliness.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

2031-03-06.seasonLabel: Thursday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: Do you fast? Give me proof of it by your works. If you see a poor man, take pity on him.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2031-03-07.seasonLabel: Friday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: Dost thou not know, dear daughter, that all the sufferings, which the soul endures, or can endure, in this life, are insufficient to punish one smallest fault, because the offence, being done to Me, who am the Infinite Good, calls for an infinite satisfaction?
quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

2031-03-08.seasonLabel: Saturday of the First Week of Lent

quote.text: He who had wished to demonstrate to us, even in His own flesh, the flesh's infirmity, by the reality of suffering, said, 'Father, remove this Your cup'; and remembering Himself, added, 'save that not my will, but Yours be done.' He was the Will and the Power of the Father: and yet, for the demonstration of the patience which was due, He gave Himself up to the Father's Will.
quote.author: Tertullian

quote.text: For that death is destroyed, and that the Cross has become the victory over it, and that it has no more power but is verily dead, this is no small proof, or rather an evident warrant, that it is despised by all Christ's disciples, and that they all take the aggressive against it and no longer fear it; but by the sign of the Cross and by faith in Christ tread it down as dead.
quote.author: St. Athanasius

2031-03-10.seasonLabel: Monday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: The whole of our treatment and exertion is concerned with the hidden man of the heart, and our warfare is directed against that adversary and foe within us, who uses ourselves as his weapons against ourselves, and, most fearful of all, hands us over to the death of sin.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

2031-03-11.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: A man is born natural and physical. In baptism he becomes supernatural and theological.
quote.author: St. Lawrence of Brindisi

2031-03-12.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: Take therefore first, as an indestructible foundation, the Cross, and build upon it the other articles of the faith.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

2031-03-13.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: O sweet exchange! O unsearchable operation! O benefits surpassing all expectation! That the wickedness of many should be hid in a single righteous One, and that the righteousness of One should justify many transgressors!
quote.author: Author of the Epistle to Diognetus

2031-03-14.seasonLabel: Friday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: Whoever is desirous of great reward and everlasting salvation, of high knowledge and deep wisdom, of standing erect in joy and sorrow, of possessing full security against all evil, whoever wishes to drink a draught of Thy bitter Passion, and Thy singular sweetness, must carry Thee at all times, O crucified Jesus, before the eyes of his heart.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2031-03-15.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Second Week of Lent

quote.text: From this love-o'erflowing Passion, I take what fully makes up for the insufficiency of my own small merits; herein lies my complete justification; to meditate on this Passion, I call eternal wisdom, the perfection of all knowledge, the riches of all salvation, an entire satisfaction of all desert; it casts me down in prosperity, it raises me up in adversity, it keeps me in an even balance between this world's weal and woe, and guards me against all evil in complete security.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

quote.text: O Lord and Master of my life, give me not the spirit of sloth, of despondency, of ambition, or of idle talking; but bestow on me, Thy servant, the spirit of chastity, of humility, of patience, and of love.
quote.author: St. Ephrem the Syrian

2031-03-17.seasonLabel: Monday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: Let us then not be ashamed of the Cross of our Saviour, but rather glory in it.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Jerusalem

2031-03-18.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Third Week of Lent

alternatives.name: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: More easily through fasting does prayer penetrate heaven.
quote.author: St. Isidore of Seville

2031-03-19.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Third Week of Lent
2031-03-19.celebration: St. Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary

quote.text: A soul does not benefit as it should from the sacrament of confession if it is not humble. Pride keeps it in darkness. The soul neither knows how, nor is it willing, to probe with precision the depths of its own misery. It puts on a mask and avoids everything that might bring it recovery.
quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

2031-03-20.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: Oh, what a sure path is the way of Thy Passion, along the way of truth, up to the very pinnacle of all perfection.
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2031-03-21.seasonLabel: Friday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: In the distribution of alms and care of the poor, let our Christian fast-times be fat and abound; and let each bestow on the weak and destitute those dainties which he denies himself.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

2031-03-22.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Third Week of Lent

quote.text: O sweet Jesus, wound my heart, that tears of penitence and love may be my food night and day, and bring me entirely to thee; that my heart may ever be habitable for thee, and my conversation pleasing and acceptable to thee; and the end of my life so praiseworthy, that after the close of this life, I may deserve to praise thee with all thy Saints forever.
quote.author: St. Bridget of Sweden

quote.text: For the wilderness is the mother of quiet; it is a calm and a harbor, delivering us from all turmoils.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2031-03-24.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: Behold, assiduous meditation on My Passion makes out of a simple man a master of high knowledge; truly it is a living book in which everything is to be found. How right blessed is that man who has it ever before his eyes and studies it!
quote.author: Bl. Henry Suso

2031-03-25.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: Offer your soul to God, make him an oblation of your fasting, so that your soul may be a pure offering, a holy sacrifice, a living victim, remaining your own and at the same time made over to God. Whoever fails to give this to God will not be excused, for if you are to give him yourself you are never without the means of giving.
quote.author: St. Peter Chrysologus

2031-03-26.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: Go and sit in your cell and your cell will teach you everything.
quote.author: Abba Moses

2031-03-27.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: So it behoves us, if we would have Christ for a frequent guest, to fill our hearts with faithful meditations on the mercy He showed in dying for us, and on His mighty power in rising again from the dead.
quote.author: St. Bernard of Clairvaux

2031-03-28.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: Strive always to prefer, not that which is easiest, but that which is most difficult; Not that which is most delectable, but that which is most unpleasing; Not that which gives most pleasure, but rather that which gives least; Not that which is restful, but that which is wearisome.
quote.author: St. John of the Cross

2031-03-29.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fourth Week of Lent

quote.text: It is only by conforming our own will to the divine one that human beings attain their true height, that they become 'divine'; only by coming out of ourselves, only in the 'yes' to God, is Adam's desire — and the desire of us all — to be completely free.
quote.author: Pope Benedict XVI

quote.text: The interior life of a just man who tends toward God and who already lives by Him is indeed the one thing necessary. To be a saint, neither intellectual culture nor great exterior activity is a requisite; it suffices that we live profoundly by God.
quote.author: Fr. Reginald Garrigou-Lagrange, O.P.

2031-03-31.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: To the cry of prayer through Christ crucified, by Whose blood we are purged of the filth of vice, do I first invite the reader, lest perchance he should believe that it suffices to read without unction, speculate without devotion, investigate without wonder, examine without exultation, work without piety, know without love, understand without humility, be zealous without divine grace, see without wisdom divinely inspired.
quote.author: St. Bonaventure

2031-04-01.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: I believe no happiness can be found worthy to be compared with that of a soul in Purgatory except that of the saints in Paradise; and day by day this happiness grows as God flows into these souls, more and more as the hindrance to His entrance is consumed.
quote.author: St. Catherine of Genoa

2031-04-02.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: The motive for loving God is God Himself.
quote.author: St. Bernard of Clairvaux

2031-04-03.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: Let us always meet each other with a smile, for the smile is the beginning of love.
quote.author: St. Teresa of Calcutta

2031-04-04.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: He can no longer have God for his Father, who has not the Church for his mother.
quote.author: St. Cyprian of Carthage

2031-04-05.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Lent

quote.text: The circle returns upon itself and is bound. The cross opens its arms to the four winds; it is a signpost for free travellers.
quote.author: G. K. Chesterton

2031-04-06.celebration: Palm Sunday of the Passion of the Lord

quote.text: Of all the practices of the spiritual life purity of heart stands highest, and rightly, for it is the end and reward of all our labours, and is found only with those who live truly according to the spirit and as good religious.
quote.author: St. Albert the Great

quote.text: If, dearly beloved, we comprehend faithfully and wisely the beginning of our creation, we shall find that man was made in God's image, to the end that he might imitate his Creator, and that our race attains its highest natural dignity, by the form of the Divine goodness being reflected in us, as in a mirror.
quote.author: St. Leo the Great

quote.text: As often as this life's idle show tries to charm you; as often as you see in the world some vain pomp, transport yourself in mind to Paradise, essay to be now what you will be hereafter.
quote.author: St. Jerome

quote.text: Delicate is he still to whom the fatherland is sweet; strong already, he for whom every soil is a fatherland; but perfect, he for whom the whole world is exile.
quote.author: Hugh of St. Victor

readingOptions.label: Chrism Mass (morning)

quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

2031-04-11.celebration: Good Friday of the Passion of the Lord

quote.text: When God thus encounters no resistance, He does His own will in the soul, drawing it to Himself and into Himself.
quote.author: Johannes Tauler

quote.author: St. Boethius

quote.author: St. Athanasius

2031-04-14.seasonLabel: Monday within the Octave of Easter

quote.text: Hence, there is no doubt that there exists a being, than which nothing greater can be conceived, and it exists both in the understanding and in reality.
quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

quote.text: We are an Easter People and Alleluia is our song!
quote.author: St. John Paul II

2031-04-16.seasonLabel: Wednesday within the Octave of Easter

quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

2031-04-18.seasonLabel: Friday within the Octave of Easter

quote.text: I am love and Mercy Itself. There is no misery that could be a match for My mercy, neither will misery exhaust it, because as it is being granted—it increases. The soul that trusts in My mercy is most fortunate, because I Myself take care of it.
quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

2031-04-19.seasonLabel: Saturday within the Octave of Easter

quote.text: Moreover, in the Catholic Church itself, all possible care must be taken, that we hold that faith which has been believed everywhere, always, by all. For that is truly and in the strictest sense Catholic, which, as the name itself and the reason of the thing declare, comprehends all universally. This rule we shall observe if we follow universality, antiquity, consent.
quote.author: St. Vincent of Lérins

2031-04-20.celebration: Divine Mercy Sunday (Second Sunday of Easter)

quote.author: G. K. Chesterton

2031-04-21.seasonLabel: Monday of the Second Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Anselm, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: Do not be afraid of Christ! He takes nothing away, and he gives you everything.
quote.author: Pope Benedict XVI

2031-04-22.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Second Week of Easter

quote.text: And so, Lord, do thou, who dost give understanding to faith, give me, so far as thou knowest it to be profitable, to understand that thou art as we believe; and that thou art that which we believe.
quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

2031-04-23.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Second Week of Easter

quote.author: St. Leo the Great

2031-04-24.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Second Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen, Priest and Martyr

alternatives.name: St. Fidelis of Sigmaringen, Priest and Martyr

quote.text: For thus we have been enriched by His poverty, the human nature having been brought up in Him to a God-befitting dignity, and established on thrones beyond all things.
quote.author: St. Cyril of Alexandria

2031-04-25.seasonLabel: Friday of the Second Week of Easter

quote.text: This is a Feast of feasts and a Solemnity of solemnities as far exalted above all others (not only those which are merely human and creep on the ground, but even those which are of Christ Himself, and are celebrated in His honour) as the Sun is above the stars.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

2031-04-26.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Second Week of Easter

quote.text: Hell took a body, and met God face to face. It took earth, and encountered Heaven.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

quote.text: This is the Halleluia which we sing, which, as you know, meaneth, Praise ye the Lord. Therefore that period is before the Lord's Resurrection, this, after His Resurrection: by which time is signified the future hope which as yet we have not: for what we represent after the Lord's Resurrection, we shall have after our own.
quote.author: St. Augustine of Hippo

quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

2031-04-29.celebration: St. Catherine of Siena, Virgin and Doctor

quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Pius V, Pope

quote.text: All grace flows from mercy, and the last hour abounds with mercy for us. Let no one doubt concerning the goodness of God; even if a person's sins were as dark as night, God's mercy is stronger than our misery. One thing alone is necessary: that the sinner set ajar the door of his heart, be it ever so little, to let in a ray of God's merciful grace, and then God will do the rest.
quote.author: St. Faustina Kowalska

2031-05-01.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Third Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Joseph the Worker

quote.text: Yesterday I was crucified with Him; today I am glorified with Him. Yesterday I died with Him; today I am quickened with Him.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nazianzus

2031-05-02.seasonLabel: Friday of the Third Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Memorial Formulary: St. Athanasius, Bishop and Doctor

quote.text: For if we too live as though dying daily, we shall not sin.
quote.author: St. Athanasius

2031-05-03.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Third Week of Easter

quote.text: We say that the Resurrection is the reconstitution of our nature in its original form.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nyssa

quote.text: Thou hast found him to be a being which is the highest of all beings, a being than which nothing better can be conceived; that this being is life itself, light, wisdom, goodness, eternal blessedness and blessed eternity; and that it is every where and always.
quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

2031-05-05.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fourth Week of Easter

quote.text: What art thou, except that which, as the highest of all beings, alone exists through itself, and creates all other things from nothing?
quote.author: St. Anselm of Canterbury

2031-05-06.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fourth Week of Easter

quote.text: No virtue, my daughter, can have life in itself except through charity and humility, which is the foster-mother and nurse of charity.
quote.author: St. Catherine of Siena

2031-05-07.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fourth Week of Easter

quote.text: He gave us Baptism, not that we should receive and depart, but that we should show the fruits of it in our after life.
quote.author: St. John Chrysostom

2031-05-08.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fourth Week of Easter

quote.text: On this hungering step, the soul is nourished upon love; for, even as is its hunger, so is its abundance.
quote.author: St. John of the Cross

2031-05-09.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fourth Week of Easter

quote.text: Thus there is in us the principle of all excellence, all virtue and wisdom, and every higher thing that we conceive: but pre-eminent among all is the fact that we are free from necessity, and not in bondage to any natural power, but have decision in our own power as we please; for virtue is a voluntary thing, subject to no dominion: that which is the result of compulsion and force cannot be virtue.
quote.author: St. Gregory of Nyssa

2031-05-10.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fourth Week of Easter

unavailableFormularies.celebrationName: St. John of Ávila, Priest and Doctor

alternatives.name: St. John of Ávila, Priest and Doctor

quote.text: As soon as some infirmity overtakes him, a sick man should receive the Body and Blood of Christ, humbly and devoutly ask the presbyters for blessed oil, and anoint his body with it. Thus will be fulfilled in him what we read: 'Is anyone among you sick? Let him bring in the presbyters, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil. And the prayer of faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up, and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him.' See to it, brethren, that a man hastens to the health and the remission of his sins.
quote.author: St. Caesarius of Arles

quote.text: The souls who are in Purgatory cannot, as I understand, choose but be there, and this is by God's ordinance who therein has done justly. They cannot turn their thoughts back to themselves, nor can they say, "Such sins I have committed for which I deserve to be here", nor, "I would that I had not committed them for then I would go now to Paradise."
quote.author: St. Catherine of Genoa

2031-05-12.seasonLabel: Monday of the Fifth Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: Sts. Nereus and Achilleus, Martyrs
Optional Memorial: St. Pancras, Martyr

quote.text: Therefore, about to build, first set the foundation of history, then, through typological signification, raise the fabric of the mind into the citadel of faith.
quote.author: Hugh of St. Victor

2031-05-13.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Fifth Week of Easter

quote.text: Since, relative to our life on earth, the world is itself a ladder for ascending to God, we find here certain traces of His hand, certain images, some corporeal, some spiritual, some temporal, some aeviternal; consequently some outside us, some inside.
quote.author: St. Bonaventure

2031-05-14.seasonLabel: Wednesday of the Fifth Week of Easter

quote.text: The world was not conceived by chance and without reason, but for an useful end and for the great advantage of all beings, since it is really the school where reasonable souls exercise themselves, the training ground where they learn to know God.
quote.author: St. Basil the Great

2031-05-15.seasonLabel: Thursday of the Fifth Week of Easter

quote.text: Unto this Darkness which is beyond Light we pray that we may come, and may attain unto vision through the loss of sight and knowledge.
quote.author: (Pseudo-Dionysius)

2031-05-16.seasonLabel: Friday of the Fifth Week of Easter

quote.text: Without faith it is impossible to be saved.
quote.author: St. John of Damascus

2031-05-17.seasonLabel: Saturday of the Fifth Week of Easter

quote.text: For progress requires that the subject be enlarged in itself, alteration, that it be transformed into something else. The intelligence, then, the knowledge, the wisdom, as well of individuals as of all, as well of one man as of the whole Church, ought, in the course of ages and centuries, to increase and make much and vigorous progress; but yet only in its own kind; that is to say, in the same doctrine, in the same sense, and in the same meaning.
quote.author: St. Vincent of Lérins

quote.text: Our God was not satisfied to be among us only by means of the inestimable mystery of the incarnation, by means of which God became man to allow mankind to share in his divine nature, but wanted to go further in an incomprehensible and infallible manner by means of the most divine sacrament of the altar in which truthfully speaking God is with us.
quote.author: St. Lawrence of Brindisi

2031-05-19.seasonLabel: Monday of the Sixth Week of Easter

quote.text: For a most perfect mediator exercises the most perfect mediation possible in regard to some person for whom he mediates. Thus Christ exercised a most perfect act of mediation in regard to some person for whom He was Mediator. In regard to no person did He have a more exalted relationship than to Mary. Such, however, would not have been true had He not preserved Her from original sin.
quote.author: Bl. John Duns Scotus

2031-05-20.seasonLabel: Tuesday of the Sixth Week of Easter

readingOptions.label: Optional Memorial: St. Bernardine of Siena, Priest

quote.text: Our God is everywhere present, wholly everywhere; not confined to any place. 2031-12-30.seasonLabel: Sixth Day within the Octave of Christmas

quote.text: Nothing was so necessary for raising our hope as to show us how deeply God loved us. And what could afford us a stronger proof of this than that the Son of God should become a partner with us of human nature?
quote.author: St. Thomas Aquinas

2031-12-31.seasonLabel: Seventh Day within the Octave of Christmas

quote.text: For He was made man that we might be made God.
quote.author: St. Athanasius
